# Clouseau

Clouseau also provides a centrally maintained local agent skill and signed review
receipts. Agent-only installation is independent of CI: it uses authenticated
coding harnesses and creates no Actions configuration or provider secrets.
Inside Claude Code, Codex or opencode the calling agent supplies the review
sessions (`--agent`); the headless `--harness` form is for a plain terminal.
Local AI review runs regardless of coverage percentage or availability and keeps
its quality verdict separate from real verification results. Opted-in CI verifies
an enrolled runner's passing AI receipt without repeating the review, then still
requires its own tests and exact coverage before approval/merge. See
[local review, installation and trust boundaries](docs/local-review.md).
New to Clouseau? Start with the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md).
How a receipt stays valid across engine revisions: [receipt compatibility](docs/receipt-compatibility.md).
Every refusal or hold notice names its cause class and numbered next steps: [notices and their causes](docs/notices.md).
Consumers without accepted recipe/enrollment/workflows use the separate
[initial owner-authorized trust installation](docs/initial-installation.md).
Its signed evidence cannot approve ordinary changes or automatically merge.
Clouseau's own accepted-policy bootstrap and native coverage diagnostics are
documented in [self-review](docs/self-review.md).

Shared coverage gates and evidence-led AI pull request approval for GitHub Actions.
Clouseau owns the PR intent review process: check whether a change is needed,
compare it with repository contracts and precedent, request the owner's second
opinion when necessary, and approve and arm auto-merge only after every technical
requirement passes. The initial implementation was extracted from Colombo.

Version 2 implements the [change acceptance protocol](docs/change-acceptance.md):
product fit, need and proportionality; nine-factor technical findings; independent
source investigations; a persistent evidence ledger; bounded repairs; and native
protected auto-merge. Humans decide genuine purpose and authority questions.
Technical uncertainty goes to automated investigation and cannot be waived by
an intent comment. Version 1 remains explicit compatibility for existing pins.

## Ownership

Clouseau contains the coverage checker, regression tests, PR intent review rules,
DeepSeek integration, approval controller, and reusable composite action.
Each consuming repository keeps its build/test commands, a configuration file,
and its own purpose, contracts, acceptance criteria, and manual-review owner.
There is no application-specific deployment infrastructure in Clouseau.

## Operations

Automatic CI integrations reference the small `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main`
bootstrap, so it always follows the latest protected main (the engine is resolved from protected
main at run time with the repository's secrets, so a commit pin on the bootstrap adds little and
only goes stale). It selects protected Clouseau main,
freezes its SHA and computes its digest. Every engine job checks out that SHA
and invokes the local action with the same trusted outputs. Normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest update; existing full-commit references keep working. See [automatic CI upgrades](docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
for source authorization, failure behavior and exact local-receipt compatibility.
Legacy fixed installations may still use `gaulatti/clouseau@FULL_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA`;
upgrading those installations requires a reviewed PR. See `examples/colombo.json`
for the version 2 policy configuration.

| Operation | Inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `test` | none | Run Clouseau's Node regression suite |
| `coverage` | Accepted-base v2 `coverage-config`, or legacy `coverage-report` + `source-directory` with optional `coverage-format` | Require exact, nonempty 100% native application line and branch coverage; the two input forms are mutually exclusive. A repository can opt in to [changed-line coverage](docs/changed-line-coverage.md) with `coverage.mode` in its protected config plus `coverage-base-ref` and `coverage-baseline`, or in [declared coverage](docs/declared-coverage.md) (`"declared"`: enforce the minimums the client's `package.json` declares at the base revision; needs `coverage-base-ref` only) |
| `await-verification` | `config`, `pull-request` for non-PR events | Wait for the exact-head PR verification run without deadlocking a single-slot runner pool: ends cleanly with `verified=false` when verification has not started within `verification_queue_grace_seconds` (default 900), to be reassessed when the verification run completes |
| `assess` | `config`, optional `pull-request`, `provider-key`, optional `ignore-receipt: 'true'` (never read the PR's receipt; for the hosted fallback after an unusable receipt) | Authenticate local quality evidence independently of technical status, or wait for verification before CI AI assessment |
| `verify-local` | `config`, eligible published signed receipt | Validate local evidence and independent CI with zero AI calls; missing or invalid evidence holds |
| `gate` | `config`, `assessment`, optional `pull-request`, optional `update-token` | Validate protection, arm auto-merge, request owner review, or approve a verified revision; under the protected `local_review.base_moved: "update"`, merge a moved base into the branch with `update-token` instead of holding ([local review](docs/local-review.md#base-moved-hold-or-update-opt-in)) |

The wait is cheap and rate-limit aware: a running verification is polled every 15 s, an absent or queued one at growing gaps (15, 30, 60, then 120 s; about 10 requests for the default grace instead of 60), and the workflow-run listing is a conditional request (`If-None-Match`; a 304 does not count against the primary limit). A 403/429 (retry-after, `x-ratelimit-remaining`/`reset`, secondary or abuse limit) is retried with bounded exponential backoff and jitter that respects the stated reset. If the budget stays exhausted past the bounded wait, the review ends in an explicit hold, `Held: GitHub API rate limit, will retry after <time>`, shown in the `clouseau-review-incomplete` comment (`github_rate_limit`) and in the `retry_after` output; the next verification completion or a re-run after that time reassesses the PR.

For example, a caller's coverage step supplies:

```yaml
with:
  operation: coverage
  coverage-report: coverage.json
  source-directory: src
```

The report must contain every compiled application path, including uncovered
code. Vendor/dependency coverage cannot mask application gaps. Counts must match
exactly; rounded percentages, missing data, or a zero branch total fail. The
caller owns instrumentation and test execution. Colombo uses Rust nightly branch
instrumentation with normal application cfgs, followed by docs and Docker tests.

For JavaScript/TypeScript, select `coverage-format: istanbul` and pass the native
`coverage-final.json` produced by c8/Istanbul. Set `source-directory` to the
original application source tree, not compiled output. Every `.ts`, `.tsx`,
`.js`, `.jsx`, `.cjs`, and `.mjs` source must appear, including unloaded modules.
Declaration-only `.d.ts` files, concrete test conventions and dependency
directories are not application sources; generated application code remains
included. The fixed inventory conventions and multi-artifact configuration are
documented in [local coverage plans](docs/local-review.md#multiple-native-coverage-artifacts).
The checker rejects omitted,
duplicate, mismatched, skipped or malformed measurements and coverage-ignore
directives. Empty statement maps require a parse-only source check: missing
native statement-counter sites are rejected, while genuine statement-free
declarations remain valid. Branch-only declarations still require native branch
measurements. This check needs Node.js and uses the declared, bundled parser;
it never executes application source or loads application Babel configuration.
It derives exact line and branch totals from native hit counters,
never from rounded summary percentages. Configure c8 `--all` over all compiled
JavaScript with source maps to measure unloaded TypeScript sources. Run real
runtime tests as well as unit tests; this format support does not replace them.
See [native empty-map validation](docs/istanbul-source-validation.md) for its
producer trust boundary, runtime dependency and parser provenance.

For Python, select `coverage-format: coveragepy` and supply the unmodified JSON
format 3 report from `coverage.py` with branch measurement enabled. See the
[native Python coverage contract](docs/python-coverage.md) for source inventory,
report generation, path binding and exact native counter validation. This reads
coverage.py's executable lines and branch decision exits, not statement
percentages or every traced transition. Empty global totals, omitted application
modules, exclusions, partial coverage and inconsistent counters fail closed.

For Go, select `coverage-format: go` and supply the `go test -coverprofile` text
profile built with `-coverpkg=./...`. Go records statements and basic blocks only, so
`lines` means statements and `branches` means basic blocks; implicit false exits and
short-circuit operands are not measured. See the [native Go coverage
contract](docs/go-coverage.md) for exact semantics, inventory and failures.

For Swift, produce LCOV with `swift test --enable-code-coverage` and `xcrun llvm-cov export -format=lcov`
and declare `source_suffixes: [".swift"]` on an `lcov` part. The toolchain records no branch outcomes, so a
pure Swift part fails the exact gate with `No branches measured`; see the [Swift coverage
recipe](docs/swift-coverage.md).

Monorepos may use the accepted-base version 2 local recipe with separate native
Istanbul, coverage.py and Go parts. `operation: coverage` accepts that recipe through
`coverage-config` and uses the shared per-part and aggregate measurement rules.
The CI gate requires each part to be complete and exact; local AI can assess
honest partial or unavailable measurements. There is no consumer-side report
merging. Legacy single-report inputs remain supported.

## Trust and permissions

Keep test execution and privileged review in separate jobs. Contributor code runs
on disposable read-only PR runners with no secrets. Assessment and gating must
check out only the protected base branch; configuration, README, and repository
contract files are read from that trusted checkout. PR patches, source, commit
messages, and tickets are untrusted evidence and never executed by the reviewer.

The `assess` job needs actions/contents/pull-requests/issues read permissions and
the repository's `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. `gate` needs contents/pull-requests/issues/
actions write permissions and must receive no provider key. Pass the
assessment output between jobs. The action cannot elevate the caller's token.
Version 1's shared model is `deepseek-flash`; changes are sent to it only after
technical verification succeeds. It assesses repository fit and supported intent,
including large test improvements. There is no file-count or line-count approval
cutoff. New product decisions and unclear scope require the owner’s judgment.
A missing or token-truncated provider completion is retried within the same
read-only assessment, using the identical evidence, at most three attempts total.
Retries wait one then two seconds. The output budget starts at 4,096 tokens and
doubles only after a token-limit truncation, capped at 16,384 tokens per request.
Every request retains its 90-second timeout. Fixed attempt/outcome/token-budget
categories are logged without model text, reasoning, patches, or credentials.
A complete verdict stops retries immediately, including second opinions,
integrity rejections, and invalid or wrong-revision evidence. HTTP failures,
network/decoding errors, unknown terminal finish reasons, and exhausted retries
fail closed and require a second opinion. The provider health probe is unchanged. AI must also support test integrity with evidence about assertions
and failure cases. Detected test fakery blocks approval, including after an intent
confirmation. Coverage percentages alone cannot satisfy that assessment. No numerical confidence score grants approval.

`sensitive_paths` lists additional paths the consumer explicitly protects with
owner confirmation. The example leaves it empty; ordinary test, dependency,
and infrastructure paths are assessed by AI rather than rejected by filename.
The configured verification workflow, review controls, and repository-purpose
contract remain protected. Their changes still receive an AI integrity assessment
and require explicit owner confirmation.

`managed_agents` is an opt-in, default-off exception for one protected path: an
`AGENTS.md` change whose managed block is byte-identical to a digest enrolled in the
protected configuration, with every byte outside the block unchanged, is not held for
owner confirmation. See [managed-standard AGENTS.md updates](docs/managed-agents.md).

`exact_revert` is an opt-in, default-off exception for one review: a PR whose resulting tree is
byte-identical to an earlier first-parent tree of the base history, within a window set in the protected
configuration, is accepted without a fresh AI review; protected controls still need the exact-head owner
confirmation and verification is unchanged. See [exact revert acceptance](docs/exact-revert.md).

The native protected merge path requires active effective base-branch rules: strict required
checks for the configured verification job and native `approve-and-merge` job
from GitHub Actions, a fresh approving review, no deletion, and no force pushes. The installing
administrator must also verify no bypass actors. Repository auto-merge and Actions
approving reviews must be enabled for automatic merge. Runtime tokens do not get administration access.

Missing or insufficient repository settings are a notice, never a failure. The review, acceptance
record and approval complete and the job succeeds, but Clouseau neither arms nor performs the
merge. It posts one fixed-text comment, updated in place, naming only bounded classes: auto-merge
disabled, main not protected, required checks missing, approval freshness missing, up-to-date
missing, force-push+deletion protection missing. Security reasoning: without protection the bot
approval cannot make an unsafe merge more possible than it already is, so it is harmless, while
merging or arming auto-merge on insufficient protection stays forbidden. API errors other than a
reported gap still fail.

Protocol v2 also supports explicit `"merge_mode": "manual"` in accepted base
configuration. Repository auto-merge must be disabled in this mode, including
for owner-authored PRs. Tests, exact coverage, review, source binding and
current-head code-owner approval for external contributors when CODEOWNERS is configured remain mandatory.
Available branch protection is still enforced. Only GitHub's specific HTTP 403
private-plan upgrade response, together with verified private visibility and an
unprotected branch, permits approval without host-enforced protection. Generic
permission failures, unavailable APIs, public unprotected repositories and
incomplete available rules fail closed. The summary states when GitHub cannot
enforce the checks; trusted maintainers must honor them before manually merging.
The controller never merges or dispatches deployment in manual mode.

This repository explicitly selects `"merge_mode": "automatic"` for strict owner-only automation:
CODEOWNERS must exist on the accepted base and the author must own every affected
path. The normal protected native flow is unchanged. On the exact unavailable
private-plan condition above, native repository auto-merge stays disabled while
the validated acceptance controller can atomically fast-forward the exact base
to the reviewed head, with paired source/base compare-and-swap and no force.
This supports same-repository branches with an up-to-date head only; other
contributions remain manual. Missing/stale reviews, failed full verification or
coverage, changed revisions and API errors cannot authorize that write. This is
controller-enforced delivery, not unavailable native branch protection. See
[the complete private-plan contract](docs/change-acceptance.md#controller-enforced-owner-merge-on-an-unavailable-private-plan),
including deployment-trigger limitations. Omitting `merge_mode` preserves the
existing native flow and optional CODEOWNERS behavior.

Manual decisions assign the PR to `manual_reviewer` and request that person's
review. Owner-authored PRs use assignment without an invalid self-review request.
The owner can comment `/approve-intent FULL_HEAD_SHA`; this confirms intent only.
An owner confirmation can carry the actual accepted requirement, rather than
leaving investigators to infer it from a revision alone:

```text
/approve-intent FULL_HEAD_SHA

Accepted purpose:
Describe the accepted outcome and its boundaries.
```

Clouseau authenticates the configured owner and current permission, binds the
literal requirement to that revision and revalidates it before writing. Ordinary
PR prose remains untrusted; every mechanism still earns its own justification.
An agent delegated to install an accepted scope may record these confirmations
on the owner's behalf through its repairs without repeated approval prompts.
All tests and exact coverage remain mandatory. Changes invalidate the decision.
The Actions bot cannot approve its own PR; it needs an independent human review.
First-time fork workflow authorization remains GitHub's responsibility.

The PR report starts with a plain-language decision, one conservative scorecard,
and one entry per causal technical finding. Each entry shows its consequence,
blocking score, affected area, evidence and required outcome. Reviewer
disagreements, product rework, missing evidence and owner decisions stay visible.
The lowest product scores across all material changes and both reviewers are
shown; unrelated good scores never compensate for a failing change. Optional
findings show expected benefit and optional priority without creating a blocker.

Expand **Scoring and evidence** for the unchanged formulas, every individual
grade and explanation, both independent reviews, persistent finding history and
the evidence register (source and line ranges). Source text is not copied into PR
comments; the complete source-bound record stays in the run's acceptance artifact.
Large audits retain lossless evidence pages. Summary
formatting uses the already validated record and makes no model requests. A
review decision never claims that merge, deployment or live verification finished.

The display regression includes the actual public Palazzo #27 review, linked to
its immutable signed evidence. Its original comment contains 36,564 characters;
5,388 remain visible with evidence sections closed. The new overview contains
948 visible characters, over five times shorter, with the same approved
verdict, both reviewers' 100/100 product scores and no technical findings. This
is an offline display fixture, never a substitute for fresh review or CI evidence.

Version 2 additionally uploads `work/clouseau-acceptance*.json` as a run/attempt
bound artifact (`clouseau-acceptance-<run id>-<attempt>`) and downloads it into
`work/` in the separate approval and repair jobs. The download resolves the
artifact by run id with `src/acceptance-artifact.cjs` (a `actions/github-script`
step named `Locate this run's acceptance record`, see this repository's
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), taking the newest attempt that is not later than the
current one, because `gh run rerun --failed` re-runs only the failed approval job
as a new attempt while the successful assessment job's artifact keeps its
original attempt number. The lookup accepts only artifacts of this run id and
this revision of the workflow that have not expired; the gate still compares
the record against the assessment's digests, head, base and frozen engine.
**A consumer that copied the artifact-transport workflow must update its copy**
(add the lookup step after the engine checkout and download the name it outputs)
before a failed-jobs re-run can find the assessment; `record-transport:
job-output` consumers need only the engine update. Once the review is accepted
the merge step is safe to repeat: enabling auto-merge and submitting the approval
retry transient GitHub failures (GraphQL "Something went wrong", HTTP 5xx and
short secondary rate limits) after 2, 6 and 15 s. Validation, permission and
"not mergeable" errors fail at once with GitHub's message. If the transient
failure persists the job fails with a notice that the review was already
accepted and that re-running the failed job is safe and repeats no AI review. Select examiner, challenger and grader explicitly in `acceptance`; see
[the self-hosting configuration](.github/clouseau.json). `typesafe-key` is needed
only when the explicit Jev/DeepSeek grading route is selected. Failure never
silently changes that choice. A separate repair job receives an independent
author token through `repair-token`; Colombo reuses its existing deployment
token. Neither the approval job nor AI inspection receives that author token. The repair
job requires a trusted GitHub head repository matching the base repository before
loading the author credential; the writer independently rechecks that identity.
Only purpose/authority decisions can use owner confirmation in version 2.

The consumer must retain PR, metadata-only target, comment, and manual workflow
entry points and PR-level concurrency. The controller validates the exact latest
PR-event run, revision, verification job, and named steps from configuration.
The read-only `assess` job waits for the PR verification run to finish before
calling AI. That wait occupies a runner, and a verification job that is queued
behind it on a single-slot pool can never start, so the wait is bounded by
progress (see "Waiting for verification" in `docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md`). Allow 70 minutes for this job when verification can take 60 minutes.
The separate native job named `approve-and-merge` calls `gate`; it must run on
`pull_request_target` and fail if assessment fails, intent is missing, integrity
is rejected, or technical evidence is incomplete. Use `always()` with `needs`
so a failed assessment cannot silently skip the required gate. In other event
contexts, use a different job name to avoid a skipped duplicate required check.
The `native-gate` and `wait-for-verification` action inputs default to `true`.

The native job summary preserves detailed reasons; no additional API check is
created in native mode. A `GITHUB_TOKEN` API check can attach to another run's
suite and is insufficient as the required approval result for this flow. Comment/manual handlers call
`request-reassessment` with actions write and contents/pull-requests read access;
they rerun the current revision's existing `pull_request_target` run. Its test job
is skipped, so confirming intent does not rebuild the container. The handler
validates maintainer permission and exact comment SHA before requesting a rerun.

Run `finalize` in a separate job after the native gate succeeds, with actions
write and contents/pull-requests read access and no provider key. Guard that job
on the gate's explicit result (`!cancelled() && needs.approve-and-merge.result == 'success'`),
not on GitHub's implicit success: a receipt skips the hosted review job it also needs. Auto-merge must
wait for the required gate job to finish, so deployment handoff cannot run inside
that gate. A provider diagnostic remains read-only and never approves a PR.

`deployment` is either `null` or an explicit workflow and path list. For a bot
merge touching those paths, Clouseau dispatches that existing workflow because
`GITHUB_TOKEN` merges suppress push-triggered workflows. It verifies main still
points at the merged revision. Deployment health, staged rollout, smoke tests,
bake windows, and ticket closure remain separate delivery work.

## Development

```sh
node --test src/*.test.cjs
```

Clouseau's own CI also requires exactly 100% line and branch coverage across
all production JavaScript modules. New source files are included
even when no test imports them. Test code is outside the production scope;
there are no exclusions for production failure paths or rounded thresholds.

To run the same gate locally with Node 22:

```sh
./scripts/verify-coverage
```

Clouseau needs only Node. One integration test runs a fixture Python application
under real coverage.py to prove the `coveragepy` adapter against live output, so
install `requirements-test.txt` (coverage.py 7.13.0) to run the whole suite. The
coverage gate itself is `bin/coverage-gate.cjs`
(`check REPORT SOURCE_DIRECTORY [llvm|istanbul|coveragepy|go]` or
`plan ACCEPTED_CONFIG [DIRECTORY]`), so reviewing a Python application requires
Python only for that application's own tests.

Successful native Node runs print compact outcomes and retain complete same-run
traces with per-run hashes; see [native verification traces](docs/native-verification.md).

CI also exercises the packaged composite action and verifies both passing and
failing coverage reports. No provider credential is needed for regression tests.
The new repository's wiki is not initialized; operational documentation lives
here until a wiki is available.

## Live model evaluations

The `evaluate-review` operation calls the real provider with three committed
synthetic review contexts. Maintenance must qualify, unrelated product scope
must request an owner decision, and test-specific validation bypasses must block
approval. A wrong or unavailable decision fails the evaluation. The GitHub and
technical-readiness inputs are fixtures; these evaluations validate model judgment,
not actual test execution or an end-to-end PR merge. The maintenance case injects
one synthetic truncated completion before calling the real provider to verify
automatic recovery within the same assessment. Logs identify that injection
explicitly; it is not evidence of a naturally occurring provider outage. Controller regression tests
use simulated provider decisions separately. Run live evaluations only in a
read-only diagnostic job with the provider key and no repository write token.

## Wiki maintenance after deployment

The [shared wiki policy](policy/wiki-maintenance.md) grounds documentation in the
exact deployment source revision and current wiki. A read-only job plans the
complete page set, generates each page against that common plan, validates links
and navigation, and independently fact-checks every proposed page, including
retained claims. Existing wiki prose can be stale; production control flow takes
precedence. The full bundle must pass before it becomes a publishable artifact.

Planning and writing use DeepSeek Flash; the independent factual checker uses
DeepSeek V4 Pro with low reasoning effort; Flash uses non-thinking mode at
temperature zero. DeepSeek's
[beta strict function-return format](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/tool_calls/)
provides separate schemas for planning, the exact requested page, and factual
review. The sole return name is `wiki_result`. Its arguments are parsed as data;
no model-selected function is executed. Plain-text answers, unknown return names,
multiple returns, and incomplete results fail closed. The factual checker uses
automatic tool choice because the provider forbids forced choices in thinking
mode; a plain answer still fails validation. Token truncation retries
use identical evidence and schemas, at most three attempts with 4,096/8,192/16,384
output tokens and 90-second deadlines. PR review keeps its existing API and
reasoning policy.

Each page receives a dedicated factual audit with the complete source map and
the other proposed pages for consistency. The combined factual report is a fixed
checklist keyed by the planned pages. Each page
has one source reference, a findings string limited to 2,000 characters, and a
supported verdict emitted last. Every page must be supported with no unresolved
findings; contradictory verdicts are rejected. This avoids unbounded evidence
arrays while retaining an independent judgment for every updated page.

Source references select controller-assigned `path:Lnumber` IDs. The native
response schema restricts paths to actual source filenames; shortened basenames
are not accepted. The source map preserves exact lines, including blanks.
Local validation rejects invented IDs, blank citations, and missing page checks.
The model cannot substitute quotation text.
This is an AI quality gate rather than a proof of semantic correctness;
documentation still needs correction when new evidence reveals an error.

A rejected factual draft may receive up to three correction passes from actionable findings.
Only pages with findings are regenerated; other page bytes are preserved. The
complete corrected batch must differ, pass structural/link validation again,
and receive a fresh supporting factual verdict. No previously rejected text is
resubmitted, including cycles between drafts. Missing findings or an exhausted
correction budget stops publication. The
read-only `evaluate-wiki` operation disables correction and calls the real model
on supported authentication and shared-refresh documents plus deliberate
denial/unavailability and FTP-only-refresh falsehoods. Provider, schema, or citation failures cannot count as a successful
negative result.

Live evaluation case diagnostics are saved at `wiki-plan.json.evaluation.json`,
including when a positive or negative control fails. Structured generation
diagnostics are saved beside the plan at
`wiki-plan.json.diagnostic.json`. Rejected planning values are retained before
any generation. Factual diagnostics contain each reviewed draft, findings, and
its immutable source-line map. Consumers should upload diagnostics even when
planning fails. No provider credentials or raw transport bodies are stored.

A separate publisher receives no model key or deployment credentials. It downloads
only its own workflow run's artifact and independently verifies the repository,
source SHA, wiki base SHA, run ID, and the expected main workflow's completed
successful deployment job. Draft generation can skip deployment verification;
publication never can. Generation needs `actions: read` and `contents: read`.
Only publication needs `contents: write` and a Git-authenticated wiki checkout.

Consumer `.github/clouseau-wiki.json` specifies every field explicitly:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "source_paths": ["README.md", "src/", "migrations/", "Dockerfile", "compose.yaml", "Makefile", "scripts/", ".env.example", ".github/workflows/"],
  "deployment_workflow": "backend-deploy.yml",
  "deployment_job": "deploy",
  "wiki_branch": "master"
}
```

Only committed text in those paths is read. Real `.env` files and agent-rule paths
are refused; wiki agent instructions are excluded from model context. The wiki
must be a clean, initialized Git checkout. Pages are flat Markdown filenames,
including Home, `_Sidebar`, and `_Footer`; the model cannot change configuration,
edit `AGENTS.md`, or delete pages. Local limits are twenty pages, 128,000 bytes per
page, 512,000 bytes per bundle, 300 source files, and 1,000,000 bytes per complete
request. Nothing is silently truncated. Unsafe paths, duplicate/ambiguous names,
broken internal links, orphaned new pages, unsupported link syntax, and unclosed
code fences fail validation.

Publication uses a private temporary Git index, never model-directed filesystem
writes. All pages and the `.clouseau-deployment.json` source/run receipt form one
commit. A changed remote wiki base or rejected non-force push publishes nothing;
concurrent human edits are never rebased or overwritten. A repeated source SHA
is idempotent. A new revision with no Markdown changes records a truthful audit
receipt. Serialize deployment and documentation together to prevent a later
release from overtaking documentation. Documentation failure leaves the completed
deployment intact and makes the workflow fail visibly; it does not roll back or
claim external service health, running image bytes, or terminal upload delivery.


### Review reliability and provider qualification

Reviews retain fixed/dismissed findings across pushes and explicitly inventory
inspected, excluded and missing evidence. Missing material context prevents
approval. When protected-base CODEOWNERS exists, protocol v2 enables automatic merge only for code-owner-authored PRs;
other contributions require current-head code-owner approval and manual merge.
Confirmed absence leaves that ownership gate inactive; existing invalid files or
unavailable ownership evidence still block. Other acceptance gates are unchanged.
See [the review contract](docs/change-acceptance.md#review-convergence-and-completeness).

The frozen qualification corpus in `test/acceptance-cases.cjs` includes clean
maintenance, a real executable zero-body regression, product drift, unnecessary
machinery, deceptive tests, a dismissed false allegation and unavailable material
context. Each case has an expected disposition and an evidence-based rationale.
A blocking verdict on an unrelated issue does not qualify the known-defect case.

`node test/evaluate-acceptance.cjs` performs live judgment qualification using the
existing provider credentials and routes. `CLOUSEAU_EVALUATION_GRADERS` selects
`deepseek`, `typesafe` or `routed` (comma-separated for comparisons). Optional
`CLOUSEAU_EVALUATION_CASES` selects named diagnostic cases; such a partial run does
not qualify a replacement. Output records the corpus and protocol fingerprints,
selected cases, route, literal evidence, responses and bounded request usage.
At most 64 provider requests, including historical replay usage, are permitted.
Completed negative decisions are retained, never retried to seek approval. Only unusable
provider output (HTTP 5xx or 429, network error, invalid tool call, malformed JSON, a report that
fails controller validation) is asked again with the identical prompt, at most twice, and recorded.

Recorded-response tests exercise transport parsing, validation, history and
scoring without calling a model. They are deterministic software evidence,
not evidence of a replacement model's review quality. Provider changes require
a complete live corpus qualification against the same frozen inputs and expected
outcomes; no provider is switched automatically by these tests. Replay is allowed
only for unchanged source/policy/routing inputs and is labeled separately from
new live calls. Qualification fixtures do not establish a genuine PR merge.

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

Post-deployment wiki maintenance is a separate, already supported operation.
Source merge, deployment, live health and published documentation remain distinct
results; do not infer one from another.

Fix a clouseau refresh defect: on the `updated` path (binding "diff", the merged diff unchanged), refresh pushed a merged head whose compatibility declaration was stale. The merge brought another merged pull request's change to a declared semantic file, so the declaration's pinned hash no longer matched, and the repository's own verify failed in CI (gaulatti/clouseau#251, 2026-11-13). Owner-ordered through the orchestrating session, with the approved narrow rule.

Required:
- On the `updated` path only, after the merge and before the push, check the merged tree's declarations with the repository's own rules (the same inspect the maintainer tool's verify uses), not a copy of them.
- Applies only to a repository that carries the tooling (a compat/ manifest and a compat/declarations/ directory). Any other repository refreshes exactly as before.
- A clean tree pushes exactly as before.
- Re-pin in the same push only when the only problems are stale content pins, every stale declaration has one decision, and together they declare exactly the pull request's own changed semantic paths. In that case, replace them with one declaration with the same decision over the same files, written by the tool's own declare, commit it, re-check that the tree is clean, and push. Report the re-pin in the result.
- In every other case (another problem, which includes an unfolded base change; an undeclared change; a different path set; mixed decisions; a re-check that still fails), push nothing and name the reason. Leave the local merge in place.
- A code comment states the general invariant: `updated` never pushes a head that fails a cheap deterministic invariant of the repository. No verification recipe runs in `updated`.
- Tests for each case, docs updated, and a compatibility declaration per docs/receipt-compatibility.md.

# Local review and CI receipt reuse

The canonical `skills/clouseau` skill runs Clouseau with a locally authenticated
coding harness. Installation refreshes protected public Clouseau main into one
shared user cache and registers the skill globally. Application repositories
contain their purpose and verification recipe, not copies of the review engine.

## Separate installations

Run `bash scripts/install-agent` from Clouseau, or use bastille's managed startup
bootstrap. The installer creates only a shared source cache, user-wide skill
links and the `clouseau` launcher. It creates no Actions files, provider secrets,
CI dependencies, signing credentials or branch rules. Explicit installer
`--prefix` and `--cache-root` paths support separate user profiles and isolated
installation checks without changing a home directory.

The launcher checks source freshness before every invocation. It loads an
immutable checkout for that run and preserves modified caches or unrelated
installed skills with an explicit error. An unavailable update does not silently
activate stale code. Codex and Claude Code use their existing authenticated
account stores; Clouseau makes no direct DeepSeek/Jev requests in local mode.

## Temporary directories

A run leaves no temporary directory behind. It creates `clouseau-harness-*` for a
harness call and `clouseau-wiki-index-*` for a wiki publish in the system temp
directory. It creates `clouseau-base-*`, the clean base-revision checkout used for the
`changed_lines` coverage baseline, in the work directory
`~/.local/share/clouseau/work` (inside the CLI's state directory, created with mode
0700 when missing). Each directory is removed when the step that made it ends, on
success or error, and again when the process exits or receives SIGINT, SIGTERM or
SIGHUP (exit status 128 plus the signal number). Anything that must survive a run, such
as a resumed agent exchange, lives under the state directory, never in a temporary
directory.

The base checkout lives under the home directory because the base revision's
verification runs the repository's own recipe there, and a recipe step may bind-mount
that checkout into a container with Docker Compose. Docker VMs on macOS, such as
Colima's `default` profile, share only the home directory by default. The system temp
directory (`/var/folders/...` on macOS) is not shared, so a container started against a
checkout there would see empty mounts. No extra Colima mount is needed.

At startup the launcher also removes directories that an earlier process left behind
because it was killed outright, in both the system temp directory and the work
directory: names of exactly the form `clouseau-v8-*`, `clouseau-v8-empty-*`,
`clouseau-base-*` or `clouseau-harness-*` (prefix plus the six random characters) that
are real directories (symlinks are never followed) and were last modified more than 24
hours ago. Errors are ignored. The `clouseau-v8-*` names were left by the engine's own
coverage tests, which now remove their fixtures. A `git worktree` entry whose checkout
was removed this way is pruned by `git worktree prune`.

## Local-only repository configuration

Commit `.clouseau-local.json` on the accepted base. It is independent of GitHub
Actions and contains no provider settings:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "base_branch": "main",
  "readme": "README.md",
  "repository_policy": "AGENTS.md",
  "verification": [["npm", "run", "test:coverage"], ["npm", "run", "typecheck"]],
  "coverage": {
    "format": "istanbul",
    "report": "coverage/coverage-final.json",
    "source_directory": "src"
  }
}
```

`llvm` and `lcov` (production sources only; `DA` lines and `BRDA` branches) are also supported. A version 2 `lcov` part may add
`source_suffixes` (for example `[".swift"]`, see [changed-line coverage](changed-line-coverage.md#swift-rust-and-other-lcov-languages)) to cover
a non-JS/TS language. The shared parser requires complete, nonempty exact
line/branch counters. Commands run as argument arrays, without shell expansion.
The accepted base supplies the recipe; a change cannot weaken its own checks.
The source checkout must be committed and clean before review. Verification
artifacts should use the repository's established ignored output locations.

### Multiple native coverage artifacts

Version 2 keeps separate native reports for applications with multiple source
roots. Its `coverage` field is a nonempty array with at most 32 explicit parts:

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "base_branch": "main",
  "readme": "README.md",
  "repository_policy": "AGENTS.md",
  "verification": [
    ["python3", "-m", "coverage", "run", "--branch", "--source", "backend", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "backend/tests"],
    ["python3", "-m", "coverage", "json", "-o", "coverage/backend.json"],
    ["npm", "--prefix", "frontend", "run", "test:coverage"]
  ],
  "coverage": [
    {"format": "coveragepy", "report": "coverage/backend.json", "source_directory": "backend"},
    {"format": "istanbul", "report": "frontend/coverage/coverage-final.json", "source_directory": "frontend/app"}
  ]
}
```

Only the six documented top-level fields are accepted in version 2: `version`,
`base_branch`, `readme`, `repository_policy`, `verification`, and `coverage`, plus the documented optional fields
(`OPTIONAL_LOCAL_KEYS` in `src/coverage-plan.cjs`): today only [`review_reuse`](#reusing-answers-in-clouseau-review-opt-in),
which both versions accept. Every reader of the file checks against that one list: `readLocalConfig` (local review,
refresh and installation), `coverageParts` (strict in CI's attestation, lenient locally) and the coverage gate's own recipe
reader, which `plan`, `totals-plan`, `changed-plan` and `declared-plan` use on the base branch's file in consumer CI.
Misspelled or additional policy fields fail before local command execution and at the CI data entrypoint (the gate says
`Unknown version 2 coverage recipe field`). Each coverage part likewise accepts only its three
documented fields, plus the optional `package_directory` that only [declared coverage](declared-coverage.md#monorepos-one-declaration-per-part) reads and, for `lcov` parts only, the optional `source_suffixes` list. Version 1 keeps its existing compatibility behavior.

Adapt commands to the repository's real test suite. The runner passes argument
arrays directly, runs every command, and checks each untouched native report.
It does not generate a combined artifact or reinterpret counters. Native
measurement requires a complete application inventory and nonempty measured
lines. Local AI review records valid partial counts and unavailable, invalid or
unverified coverage honestly, then runs regardless of the percentage. It does
not label an old artifact as this run's verified coverage. CI's separate exact
coverage gate still requires 100% lines and branches for every part (unless the protected configuration opts in to [changed-line](changed-line-coverage.md) or [declared](declared-coverage.md) coverage; local status stays advisory exact either way). A genuinely
branchless part may have zero branches when another part supplies measured
branches; an entirely branchless plan fails that CI gate. One part cannot
compensate for another part's missing or uncovered data.

Report and source paths must be repository-relative. Resolved source roots must
exist and must not overlap, and report paths must be unique, including aliases.
Both recipe versions accept `source_directory: "."` for the complete repository
root, including executable root configuration and nested application sources.
A version 2 root part cannot appear alongside another part because their source
roots overlap. The canonical `.` spelling is allowed only for a source directory;
report and other paths keep their existing restrictions. A root recipe still
rejects missing native source measurements and uncovered counters.
Paths that escape the checkout fail. There is no arbitrary exclusion option.
Generated application code, executable configuration and entry points remain
in scope. Native JS/TS inventory excludes declaration-only `.d.ts` files,
`*.test.*`/`*.spec.*` files and the fixed `test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `.git`,
`node_modules` and `vendor` directories. Native coverage.py uses its documented
Python test/dependency conventions. Those non-application entries may appear in
a native report but cannot contribute passing counters.

Version 2 supports native measurement through the complete-inventory `istanbul`,
`coveragepy`, `go` and `lcov` adapters. Version 1's single-report interface, including LLVM,
remains supported. Unsupported native formats are reported as unavailable local
coverage; they do not suppress AI review or acquire invented counters. CI still
rejects unsupported formats. LLVM multi-root plans require a complete
compiled-source inventory capability and are not measured by version 2.
Go is measured only through the `go` adapter, whose lines are statements and
branches are basic blocks ([native Go coverage](go-coverage.md)).

The accepted base supplies the complete recipe in normal local review. Local
evidence records actual command outcomes, the digest of each command's complete stdout
and stderr and their tails (the last 128 characters of a command that succeeded, the last
4,096 of one that failed, with `stdout_bytes`/`stderr_bytes` stating the full length wherever a stream was cut), native counters when valid,
artifact digests and freshness, unavailable-coverage diagnostics, and the accepted
configuration digest. A nonzero command is not assumed to have failed only
because of coverage. One frozen engine checks every part throughout the review.

CI invokes the same shared verifier through `operation: coverage` with
`coverage-config`. That input accepts only a **version 2** recipe: a version 1
file fails with `Coverage gate failed: A multi-artifact coverage recipe requires
version 2`. A repository whose CI uses `coverage-config` therefore commits
`.clouseau-local.json` as version 2 with a one-element `coverage` array (the
version 1 example above is for local-only use or for the legacy
`coverage-report` + `source-directory` inputs). Supply the recipe from the exact accepted base, separately
from the candidate checkout. For example, in an unprivileged PR verification
job with no provider credentials:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
    fetch-depth: 0
- name: Read accepted coverage recipe
  env:
    BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
  run: git show "$BASE_SHA:.clouseau-local.json" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/accepted-coverage.json"
# Run the repository's actual tests and native instrumentation here.
- uses: gaulatti/clouseau@FULL_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA
  with:
    operation: coverage
    coverage-config: ${{ runner.temp }}/accepted-coverage.json
```

The coverage action reads that JSON as data and never executes its verification
commands. Do not supply proposed PR policy as the accepted recipe. Configuration
selection belongs to trusted workflow wiring; source execution, credentialed
assessment and the write-capable controller remain separate. `coverage-config`
cannot be combined with legacy `coverage-report` or `source-directory` inputs.
The legacy single-report inputs are unchanged.

Store the requirement outside the checkout, then run:

```bash
clouseau review --directory /path/to/repository --base origin/main \
  --request-file /path/to/requirement.txt --harness codex
```

Verification subprocesses and the native coverage parser receive the same
credential-filtered environment as initial installation: inherited variable names
matching `KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` or `CREDENTIAL` are removed.
Nonsecret runtime and tooling variables remain available. Repository verification
commands supply their own nonproduction fixture configuration. PEM private-key
output is rejected before it can enter AI evidence.

### Agent-driven review inside an AI harness

The headless `--harness codex|claude` form launches a separate child process per
model session. It is for a person at a plain terminal. Inside Claude Code, Codex
or opencode the calling agent supplies those sessions itself:

```bash
clouseau review --directory /path/to/repository --base origin/main \
  --request-file /path/to/requirement.txt --agent opencode
```

`--agent` accepts `claude`, `codex` or `opencode` and excludes `--harness`.
The controller still owns real verification, immutable sources, citations, grading
formulas, the finding ledger and the decision. When it needs a model session it
writes `request-NNNN.json`, the full `prompt-NNNN.txt` and `schema-NNNN.json` under
the review cache's `agent/` directory (outside the checkout), prints
`status: awaiting_agent` and exits with code 3. The agent starts a fresh subagent
or session that sees only those files, has it write a JSON answer to the request's
`answer_file`, and registers it:

```bash
clouseau respond --agent-request REQUEST_FILE --answer ANSWER_FILE --session SESSION_ID
```

The `awaiting_agent` output already prints this command with a valid, unused session identifier in place of
`SESSION_ID`, and a `session_rule` field that states the rule: 8 to 128 characters, letters, digits and `. _ : -`
only, starting with a letter or digit, never reused for another request. Any identifier that satisfies the rule may
replace the suggested one.

`prompt-NNNN.txt` is the policy text followed by the evidence, laid out over many lines instead of one line of up to hundreds of
kilobytes. The layout is applied only when printing the parsed evidence compactly gives back the original bytes exactly (so no
number or string is altered); otherwise the file is the original prompt. The request digest, the reuse key and answer
validation always use the original prompt, never the file.

The schema file is compact JSON Schema that states each repeated subschema (chiefly the
proof-ID enumeration every citation site shares) once under `$defs` and points at it with
`"$ref": "#/$defs/NAME"`; it is the same constraint as the full inline schema, a few KB
instead of hundreds. `respond` validates the answer against the request schema (the
supported subset, with only those `$defs` references, fails closed on unknown keywords), refuses a session identifier already used for
another request in the exchange, and allows three attempts per request. A rejected answer's reason is passed to the next
attempt. When an examiner or challenger drops or rewords a concern from its own earlier draft, the reason names that finding.
For a restatement under the same identifier, it also names the first field that differs (cause or obligation) and quotes the
earlier text, so the next fresh session can retain it verbatim or resolve it with current-source counterevidence. Repeating
the identical `review` command then resumes: it reuses the one recorded
verification, requires the same frozen evidence digest, replays accepted answers
and stops at the next pending session. A request whose stored digest no longer
matches stops the review rather than guessing.

An in-flight agent review is pinned to the engine revision that started it. The
launcher still refreshes protected main before every call, but a continuation of the
same head, base and requirement re-executes the recorded revision from the local
cache (`~/.cache/clouseau/revisions/<sha>`; the installer never prunes revisions, and
a pin under `~/.local/share/clouseau/pins/` is the reference that names one) and
prints one line stating the pinned revision and the newer one, once per newer revision (the pin remembers that it said so; a
still newer revision is announced again). The pinned checkout
must be an unmodified worktree of the installer's own cached source whose engine
digest equals the one recorded when the pin was made; otherwise the command fails and
nothing from it runs. A receipt is issued under the pinned revision, so CI, which
ignores a receipt whose engine differs from protected main, reviews the PR itself.
A new review (different head or requirement) uses the newest revision. Pass
`--engine latest` to drop the pin and restart on the newest revision; the pin is also
released when the review completes. A failure of the pinned engine is reported with the engine's own error message (its last 2,000
characters), not a bare exit status. `respond` needs no pinning: it validates against
the schema stored with the request.

Usage records for these sessions carry `harness` (`claude`, `codex` or `opencode`),
`execution: agent_session`, the supplied session identifier and digests of the
request, answer and stored response file. Receipt validation accepts them alongside
headless records and still requires distinct sessions for the examiner and
challenger investigation and grading phases. The controller cannot itself prove
that a subagent was isolated from the implementer, so this independence rests on
the runner's trust boundary and on the enrolled engine revision: CI accepts a
receipt only from a Clouseau revision the protected configuration enrolls, which is
where an owner decides whether to trust agent-driven receipts. The signed handoff,
`independent_ci_required` and `merge_authority: false` are unchanged.

Outside an AI harness, use `--harness claude` to run Claude Code headlessly. The controller runs real verification,
records its actual outcomes, captures immutable base/head sources and accepted
purpose, and starts separate examiner and challenger sessions. Coverage below
100%, a failing coverage command, or unavailable, malformed or unsupported
coverage does not prevent those local AI sessions. Additional source requests are bounded. Fresh
semantic grading sessions supply descriptive factor levels; the same Clouseau
code owns citations, formulas, thresholds and final decisions. No investigator
gets the implementer's conversation or the other investigator's conclusions.

The controller identifies this as a pre-PR assessment in both investigation and
grading. It requires the accepted local recipe, safe complete immutable source
and meaningful evidence for the changed behavior. Coverage percentage or
unavailable coverage alone does not force a failing AI quality verdict; actual
behavioral defects, deceptive tests and missing material evidence still do. The
review never rewrites failed or unavailable verification into a test pass.

New and cached CLI results identify `decision_scope: review_reuse_only`,
`independent_ci_required: true` and `merge_authority: false`, with local
verification and coverage status separate from the AI decision. A local
`auto_approve` verdict means passing AI quality evidence eligible for signed
reuse, not technical approval. CI audit, workflow and container execution remains
independent; a local receipt does not claim those results or authorize GitHub
approval. CI must pass every mandatory technical gate before approval or merge.

A source-line reference can be normalized only to an existing immutable catalog
block containing that line. The controller preserves the observation and reads
the literal source bytes; this correction needs no additional model request.
Unknown sources, out-of-range lines and unsupplied blocks still stop review.

Reports and response journals stay outside source control. A completed identical
input is not automatically reviewed again. Fix blocking findings, commit the
changed implementation and reassess. A negative or incomplete review never
produces an approval receipt. This initial receipt path targets a new PR without
an unresolved existing GitHub review ledger; it rejects an existing incompatible
ledger rather than dropping its findings.

## Receipt-attested verification

A receipt signed by an enrolled identity attests the repository's whole declared verification. `clouseau review` runs every command of the
accepted base `.clouseau-local.json` (plus any `--additional-checks`) and, **before spending any AI review, refuses to sign** (non-zero exit,
no receipt, no marker) unless all of the following hold on the exact head:

- every command ran and exited 0 (a tool that is not installed, such as `cargo llvm-cov` or `coverage.py`, is a refusal that names the
  command and the missing tool, never a partial signature);
- native coverage was produced by this run;
- the coverage gate CI enforces passes: exact 100%, or for the protected `coverage.mode` of `changed_lines` the changed lines and branches are
  covered with no repository-wide regression (the base revision is measured locally in a temporary clean worktree, as CI measures it), or
  for `declared` the minimums declared at the base.

Declare every check you want skipped in CI (tests, coverage, fmt, lint, frontend, infrastructure) as a command of `.clouseau-local.json`.
Without an enrolled identity nothing is signed and the review remains advisory. The signed verification record then carries
`attestation: {version, recipe, commands, coverage_mode, gate: "passed"}`; receipts issued before this change carry none, stay valid for the
AI review, and attest no verification.

In CI, `operation: attested` (inputs `config`, `github-token`; output `attested`) answers `'true'` only when the pull request's receipt passes
every check the assessment applies (signature, enrolled key and author, expiry, exact head and base, engine, signed sources against live
GitHub; under the protected `binding: "diff"` the normalized diff and the live base's recipe instead of the head, base and sources, see
[binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)) AND attests the accepted base recipe. Anything else (no marker,
expired, wrong head without that binding, old receipt, an error) is `'false'`. Gate any
workflow on it in a small job, as `examples/consumer-ci.yml` does:

```yaml
if: needs.attested.outputs.attested != 'true'   # on each test step, or on a whole job in another workflow
```

The skip is advisory; the enforcement is in the engine. When the configured `verification.job` succeeds with required steps `skipped`,
the engine accepts them only after verifying the same receipt itself in the trusted workflow; without a valid attesting receipt a skipped
required step is the failure it always was. A receipt expires (`max_age_seconds`), so re-run the workflow after expiry and the checks run;
the failure then names the receipt class (`receipt_expired` with its expiry instant) and that step, or `clouseau refresh --pr N` to renew
the receipt ([notices](notices.md#skipped-verification-step-without-an-attesting-receipt)).
The job named in `verification.job` must still exist and succeed, so keep it as a job whose steps are skipped rather than removing it.

## Evidence size

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly
the head source with every line prefixed `+` (consumers restore the identical patch). The pinned
engine seed (roughly 380 KB) is collected only when a workflow change adds or changes a
`gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main` (or an existing `@<sha>`) reference; an ordinary edit of a workflow that keeps its reference
carries no engine source, and a reviewer can still request any of it. The seed is optional context: seed files that would use the last 150,000
characters are listed in `omitted_sources` with a reason, and reviewers can still request them.
Changed files, their base and head sources and contracts are never omitted; a change that exceeds
the cap with only that evidence is reviewed in bounded units (see "Chunked local review") unless the protected configuration disabled chunked review, in which case it fails closed.

## Enrolling a trusted runner

Consumers with neither accepted recipe nor CI policy use the separate
[explicit initial trust installation](initial-installation.md). Its frozen
owner/admin commit-comment grant and installation-only evidence cannot replace
ordinary approval or authorize automatic merge.

`clouseau init-identity` creates an Ed25519 identity outside the repository with
private file permissions. Its output contains only the public enrollment entry
and local identity-file path. Identity creation is explicit and is never part of
agent installation. The existing authenticated GitHub account supplies the
identity's `github_actor`.

An owner must install the public enrollment entry in protected CI configuration:

```json
{
  "local_review": {
    "mode": "required",
    "central_source": {"repository": "gaulatti/clouseau", "ref": "refs/heads/main"},
    "max_age_seconds": 172800,
    "keys": [{
      "id": "PUBLIC_KEY_IDENTIFIER",
      "issuer": "ENROLLED_RUNNER_IDENTIFIER",
      "github_actor": "ENROLLED_GITHUB_LOGIN",
      "public_key": "ED25519_PUBLIC_PEM",
      "revoked": false
    }]
  }
}
```

This source authorization requires the [automatic CI resolver wiring](automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
and its frozen SHA/digest; configuration alone cannot select an engine. Legacy
fixed installations instead enroll `reviewer_digest` and omit `central_source`.
The modes are exclusive, and only the central-source integration avoids recurring
release enrollment PRs.

Receipt lifetime: `issueReceipt` defaults to 48 hours (172800 seconds), and the
trust validator rejects `max_age_seconds` above 172800. Each consumer sets its
own `max_age_seconds` in its protected `.github/clouseau.json`; the example
configuration uses 172800, and consumers that still say 3600 keep one-hour
receipts until raised separately. A receipt that expires after CI skipped the
tests on its strength fails the skipped step, naming `receipt_expired` (see above). The first
[initial-installation](initial-installation.md) authorization deliberately stays
at one hour, and installation receipts are capped by it. A receipt remains bound
to the exact head SHA (or, under the protected `binding: "diff"`, to its
normalized diff), signed review history and reviewer digest, so a changed head
(or diff) invalidates it regardless of age.

Only existing protected configuration can enroll or revoke a key. A contributor
cannot authorize their own key through the proposed PR. Keys are restricted to
their enrolled native GitHub PR author. Set `revoked` or remove a key to reject
its future receipts. `optional` mode permits the separately installed CI AI
reviewer for PRs without a receipt, and for any receipt that does not verify (it is
ignored, see below). `required` mode needs no CI AI provider credentials.

Malformed, unknown-version, duplicate or mixed receipt marker claims are ignored
before any artifact is fetched, with the `malformed` notice: in `optional` mode CI
reviews the change itself, in `required` mode the outcome is `local_receipt_required`.
Do not normalize an invalid stamp; replace it with a fresh receipt.

The initial trust boundary is an enrolled maintainer workstation, including its
operator and privileged processes. The identity is not remote or hardware
attestation. A private key held by that operating-system account cannot protect
against malicious processes with equivalent account access. Such a compromise
can forge the runner's claims. Signatures protect receipt integrity and identify
the enrolled issuer; they do not mathematically prove that an LLM executed or
that its conclusions are correct. Stronger hostile-runner protection requires
an independently isolated execution/signing service and is not claimed here.

## Signed handoff

An enrolled runner selects its matching installed identity automatically. Use
`--identity /path/to/identity.json` to select explicitly when needed. The runner
requires an unmodified public Clouseau engine and the enrolled signer. CI
authorizes the exact engine separately from the signature. Legacy CI without a
trusted frozen-source selection still requires its configured digest. It records the exact Clouseau commit and binds the executable engine,
skill, scripts and policy by a SHA-256 content digest. Legacy fixed-digest installations permit identical engine content across squash
identities. [Automatic CI upgrades](automatic-ci-upgrades.md) require both the
exact selected central commit and its computed digest; no cross-version
compatibility is inferred. It verifies
the same source and installation remain unchanged before
issuing a passing receipt. Signing material is never placed in model packets,
child-process environments, project source, reports or the published artifact.
Protected review-control changes still require the separate owner-authorized
installation path; a local receipt cannot grant that authority. A current-head owner confirmation
is independently recorded and revalidated by CI when a signed review accompanies
a review-control change.

The receipt signs a domain-separated SHA-256 payload with Ed25519. It includes
the complete review record, exact repository/head/base, Clouseau and policy/config
identities, issuer/key, issuance/expiry, and a 256-bit random nonce. Publish it
before opening the PR:

```bash
clouseau publish --directory /path/to/repository --receipt /path/to/receipt.json
```

This creates a separate artifact commit and unique `clouseau-review/<nonce>` tag;
it does not change the reviewed source commit or checkout. Include the returned
`clouseau-local-review:v1` marker in the initial ready PR body. The complete
artifact follows the repository's visibility and contains reviewed source and
the requirement text; those inputs must be appropriate for publication there.

## Refreshing a pull request after its base moved

Every merge to the base leaves the other open pull requests behind it: GitHub reports `branch update needed`, and each
assessment and approval is bound to the old base, as is each receipt unless the protected `binding: "diff"` binds it to its
diff instead ([binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)). `clouseau refresh` does the author's manual routine for one
pull request, in the pull request's own checkout:

```bash
clouseau refresh --pr N --agent claude                       # inside an AI harness
clouseau refresh --pr N --harness claude                     # headless
clouseau refresh --pr N --request-file req.txt --agent claude   # an explicit requirement
```

`--request-file` is optional. Without it the requirement is the one of the last accepted (`auto_approve`) review of this
repository and branch: every accepted review stores its requirement text byte for byte as `request.txt` beside its record under
`~/.local/share/clouseau/reviews/<cache id>/`, with a `requirement.json` that binds it, and one pointer per repository and
branch (`requirements/`) names the newest. The command refuses, and asks for `--request-file`, when nothing is recorded for the
branch, when the record is unusable (pointer and record name different repositories, branches, heads or cache ids; the text no
longer hashes to the recorded digest; a part is a link, empty or over 20,000 characters), when the recorded head is not an
ancestor of the pull request head, or is already in the base (the branch name was reused after another pull request merged), or when that review also used
`--additional-checks` (they are part of its input and are not stored; pass both again). It never guesses among candidates.
Optional: `--directory`, `--identity`, `--additional-checks`, `--engine latest`. In order, and never otherwise:

1. refuse (see below), then `git fetch origin <base>`; if the pull request already contains the base tip, the receipt in the
   pull request body decides: one that still verifies for this head ends the command with `up_to_date`, any other is
   [renewed](#renewing-a-receipt-that-no-longer-verifies) (steps 3 to 5 below, no merge and no push of the branch). Under the
   protected `binding: "diff"`, when the pull request does not contain the base tip and its receipt still covers its diff, the
   base is merged and the normalized diff recomputed; if it is unchanged the merge is pushed with no review and the command
   ends with `updated` (see [Binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)); otherwise the steps
   continue on that merge;
2. check with `git merge-tree` that the merge is clean, then **merge** the base (`git merge --no-ff`, message
   `Merge origin/<base> into <branch>`). There is no rebase and no force-push anywhere in the command;
3. run the ordinary local review of the head (`clouseau review`, including its verification) with the answers reused as
   described below, and sign the receipt. The claimed title of the change is the pull request's own title (GitHub's), not the
   subject of the merge commit, which is only `Merge origin/<base> into <branch>`; a pull request with no title is refused;
4. `clouseau publish` the receipt (this pushes only the artifact tag `clouseau-review/<nonce>`);
5. replace the `clouseau-local-review:v1` marker in the pull request body (appended when there is none);
6. `git push origin HEAD:<pull request branch>`, once, as the last step.

It refuses, with a message that names the cause and before pushing anything, when: the worktree has uncommitted or untracked
changes; HEAD is not the head GitHub reports for the pull request (when the local branch only has commits on top of that head, the message
says how many are unpushed and that you must `git push` first, then refresh again); the pull request is closed, comes from a fork, is not the
checked-out branch, or is not against the configured `base_branch`; the harness is unknown or its program is not installed;
the base conflicts with the branch (the checkout is left untouched and the conflicting paths are listed); a hook refuses the
merge (it is aborted). It never pushes when the review does not pass (`repair_required`, `review_incomplete`, ...), when a
passing review produced no signed receipt (no enrolled identity), when the checkout changed during the review, when the
pull request closed or got another head during the review, or when the push is rejected (the body is then restored). After
a review that does not pass, the merge commit stays in the local branch: repair, commit and refresh again, or run `git reset
--hard <old head>` to discard it. An agent-driven refresh that returns `awaiting_agent` is repeated with the identical
command; it recognises its own merge commit (the pull request head and a commit of the base as parents), does not merge or
fetch again, and continues on the base it began with. While Clouseau main advances, the continuation runs on the engine revision
that started the exchange ([pinning](#agent-driven-review-inside-an-ai-harness)): through the `clouseau` launcher the pinned engine
receives your own `refresh` command, resumes it and finishes it (review, publication, marker, push), and its result is what you
see. If the pinned engine fails, its error message is shown.

### Binding a receipt to its diff (opt-in)

By default a receipt is bound to the exact head and base commits it reviewed, so every merge to the base voids the receipt of
every other open pull request. With the protected `local_review.binding: "diff"` in `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch,
a receipt is bound to the **change** instead: it covers a pull request when the SHA-256 of the pull request's normalized diff
equals the SHA-256 of the normalized diff in the signed record (`src/receipt-patch.cjs`). The receipt format does not change:
the signed record already carries every patch.

The normalized diff is, per changed file in path order, its path, its status and (for a rename) its previous path, and its
hunks with every hunk header reduced to `@@`, so line numbers and git's trailing section text do not count. Every other byte
of a hunk counts, context lines and whitespace included. GitHub joins two git hunks that are one unchanged line apart; that
run of exactly seven context lines between two changes is split back into its two hunks on both sides. A summarized lockfile
contributes its path and status, and its derived summary is recomputed from the live lockfile bytes and must equal the signed
one apart from the revision it names.

| | Binding absent | `binding: "diff"` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a different head commit (GitHub's branch update, a merge of the base) | `receipt_revision_head` | covered while the diff is unchanged |
| a different base commit | `receipt_revision_base` | covered while the diff is unchanged |
| signed full-file sources compared with the live repository | compared | not compared: the signed record is what was reviewed; each source must still name a signed revision |
| the repository's contracts (`readme`, `repository_policy`, for example `.github/clouseau.md` and `README.md`) | compared at the signed base, which must be the live base | compared at the **live** base: a base move that changed either voids the receipt (`receipt_source`, naming the file) |
| lines added above a hunk on the base | `receipt_source` | covered |
| any change to an added, removed or context line, or to whitespace | `receipt_source` | `receipt_source`, naming the file |
| a file added, removed or re-statused, another rename | refused | refused, unchanged |
| a compatibility declaration (`compat/declarations/<sha256>.json`) declared again after a merge | refused (its bytes changed) | covered while every declaration keeps its verdict over the same files (path, mode, deleted or not); only the content digests it pins may differ |
| a file without a GitHub patch | refused, unless the live sources prove it shows no text | refused, even an empty file or an identical rename: the live sources are not read |
| signature, enrolled key, author, expiry, repository, protected configuration and policy digests, engine and review semantics, passing decision | bound | bound, unchanged |

A compatibility declaration ([receipt compatibility](receipt-compatibility.md)) pins the full content of the semantic files
it covers. When the base gains a merged pull request that changed one of those files, merging the base makes the
declaration stale, and declaring again replaces it with a new file under a new name. Under the binding that replacement does
not void the receipt: a file added under exactly `compat/declarations/<64 hex>.json` whose whole content is a well-formed
declaration is compared by what it declares, its verdict (`compatible` or `incompatible`) and the files it covers with their
mode and whether each is deleted, and it is left out of the normalized diff. A changed verdict, a file added to or removed
from a declaration, or a declaration gained or lost voids the receipt (`receipt_source`). Any other file under that directory
(another name, another status, a body that is not one whole declaration) is an ordinary changed file. The required `verify`
job still checks every declaration against the merged tree, so a declaration whose digests do not match the code fails
there. The pull request's changed-file count still includes the declarations.

**What still voids a diff-bound receipt after a base move.** A change on the base branch to the repository's contracts
(`readme` and `repository_policy`, compared at the live base) or to the declared recipe (`.clouseau-local.json`, which the
test waiver compares at the live base) voids every open diff-bound receipt, by design: the change was judged against them. A
summarized lockfile's summary is recomputed from the live base and head lockfile bytes, so a base move that changed a
lockfile the pull request also changes voids it when the recomputed summary differs.

The test waiver follows the same binding: `operation: attested` answers `'true'` for a receipt whose diff matches and whose
signed `.clouseau-local.json` equals the live base's, so the tests are **not** rerun after a base move or an update-branch
merge. This is deliberate and has a cost: a break caused only by the base move (a semantic conflict between the reviewed change
and the new base) is found after merge, by the next run on the base. **Accepted limit:** no CI step reruns the attested tests
